title: Multi-region batch postback ordering causes hourly credit gap on invoice
text:
Multi-region batch postback ordering causes hourly credit gap on invoice

description:
Issue summary: BrightHealth AI reports a missing hourly credit row on their Feb 28 invoice after a large multi-region batch embedding job. Impact: Customer is short ~540 credits for the 02:00-03:00 UTC hourly window; this affects billing accuracy and customer trust. Environment: prod ingestion pipeline across us-east-1 and eu-west-1; batch job ID bh-20260228-embed-73. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a multi-region batch embedding job that splits shards between us-east and eu-west. 2) Confirm job completes and each region posts hourly usage postbacks independently. 3) Observe billing engine aggregation for the 02:00-03:00 UTC window — one region's postback arrived with a backdated timestamp that routed it to the previous hour and triggered a credit hold. Logs & evidence: - Customer-provided invoice snapshot (attached) showing missing credit line for 2026-02-28 02:00-03:00 UTC. - Postback payloads (anonymized) show us-east postback time: 2026-02-28T02:12:03Z, eu-west postback time: 2026-02-28T01:58:47Z. - Ingestion logs show eu-west postback processed at 02:01:05Z but with payload timestamp 01:58:47Z. - Billing-engine aggregation logs: billing-window-aggregator produced a gap for the 02:00 hour. Additional context: Customer uses Dedicated capacity with burst enabled and hourly metering granularity. The job spanned regions and used the new multi-region batching path rolled out in release v3.14.0.

comments:
2026-03-10 - Aisha Malik (Support): Opened ticket after customer provided invoice and postback traces. Requested raw postback payloads and timestamps.
2026-03-10 - Diego Moreno (SRE): Acknowledged. Assigned to SRE/ingestion to validate ordering and TTL logic for postbacks across regions.
2026-03-11 - Customer (BrightHealth AI - Marta Lopez): Provided archived postback files and job manifest. Says they saw the missing credit only after invoice finalization.
2026-03-11 - Diego Moreno (SRE): Confirmed eu-west payload contains original client timestamp that is older than processing time. Hypothesis: ingestion honors client_ts for window assignment which, combined with late arrival, assigned the data to an earlier hourly window and triggered smoothing/hold logic.
2026-03-12 - Billing (Ravi Patel): Noted aggregation treats out-of-order hourly rows as provisional until all region postbacks arrive; current finalization threshold is 7 minutes after window close. eu-west arrived 61 seconds late but with client_ts before window boundary causing misplacement.

investigation_notes:
Checked ingestion pipeline: postbacks are accepted with client_ts and processed by region; there is an ordering step that currently uses client_ts to map to hourly buckets.
Observed that eu-west postback was processed after window close but carried a client_ts that placed some rows in the previous hour, which bypassed the final aggregation for the 02:00-03:00 window.
Billing finalization threshold of 7 minutes currently only considers server processing time, not client_ts skew. If a region posts with older client_ts after finalization, rows can land in the wrong hour and be marked provisional/held.
Search for prior incidents: related behaviour surfaced in SUP-59123 (daily metering delay) but that ticket was about delayed ingestion rather than client_ts ordering.

root_cause:
Client-provided timestamps (client_ts) from multi-region batch shards can be older than processing time; billing-window finalization uses processing time thresholds. A late-arriving payload with an earlier client_ts assigned rows to a prior hourly bucket after that bucket's finalization, causing the aggregator to hold the credit and omit it from the invoice.

impact_summary:
Single customer (BrightHealth AI) missing ~540 credits on Feb 28 invoice for the 02:00-03:00 UTC hour. Potentially affects other multi-region customers using the new multi-region batching path during similar timing windows. Billing correctness and customer trust risk.

remediation_plan:
Short term: Manually apply provisional credits for BrightHealth AI for the affected hour and issue an invoice adjustment. Target ETA: 2026-03-13.
Immediate engineering mitigation: Modify billing finalizer to consider client_ts skew window (add 2-minute backfill grace) for 24 hours while investigation continues. Deploy as hotfix to prod ingestion/billing (rollout plan: canary in us-east -> eu-west). Target ETA: 2026-03-14.
Long term: Implement deterministic postback ordering and a reconciliation job that replays late client_ts rows into correct hourly buckets and auto-generates correction credits. Schedule design doc and implementation in Q2 sprint.

resolution:
Workaround: Applied manual credit adjustment to BrightHealth AI invoice on 2026-03-13 (credit memo CM-2026-03-687). Hotfix that expands finalization grace window deployed to canary on 2026-03-14. Follow-up: automation/reconciliation story created and assigned to backlog. Ticket set to Waiting on Customer for confirmation of invoice adjustment.

follow_up_actions:
Create reconciliation job story in backlog and link to this ticket.
Add e2e test for multi-region postback ordering and client_ts skew to CI.
Update meter runbook: include guidance on client_ts skew and finalizer grace period.
Monitor affected accounts for 7 days and report any further anomalies.
